coverage_summary: Scope per get_source_scope(): 3,671 model-visible files, binaries skipped, no symlink/sensitive-name exclusions; the tree is Jetty 12.0.17-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml:7) covering jetty-core (server, http, io, util, session, security, openid, http2, http3, xml, start, maven, client, proxy, fcgi, websocket, alpn, quic, jndi, plus), jetty-ee8/ee9/ee10 (servlet, webapp, security, jaspi, websocket, annotations, maven plugins, demos), jetty-home, and jetty-integrations (gcloud, hazelcast, infinispan, memcached, nosql). Note that src/test trees are NOT in the visible scope (list_files/search_code return no test paths), so test-based evidence could not be used. P1 relation scope reports a partial index: 3,565 of 3,671 files indexed (106 source files missing), ~107 omitted files, Java syntax only — containment/call/inheritance name-and-arity candidates with no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or runtime reachability; all index facts used only as navigation hints and verified against source. Areas inspected directly include ContextHandler/handler package, ResourceService/alias checkers/ResourceServlet/DefaultServlet, SecurityHandler/Constraint/authenticators/OpenID, session/cookie code, HttpURI/URIUtil/UriCompliance, HttpParser/HttpGenerator, HTTP/2 generators/session, MultiPart/MultiPartFormData, ErrorHandler, ShutdownHandler, SecuredRedirectHandler, CrossOriginHandler, XmlParser/XmlConfiguration, and the duplicated ee9/ee10 variants. Coverage is sampling-based, not exhaustive: large files (e.g. HttpURI.java 1.7k lines, HttpParser.java 2.3k lines, XmlConfiguration.java 2.1k lines, HTTP/2/3 stacks, WebSocket, QUIC, OSGi, JSP/Maven plugins) were only partially read.
limitations: No reference (fixed) version, patch, CVE/advisory text, or repository history is available in this run, so a fix-diff comparison — normally the most reliable way to identify the vulnerable code — was impossible.

Test sources are excluded from the snapshot, so tests that would exercise the vulnerable behavior or reveal expected-vs-actual behavior could not be inspected or run; no code, tests, or scanners were executed.

The P1 source-relation index is explicitly partial and syntactic only (no control/data-flow, no semantic resolution, no reachability); 106 files are missing from the index, and index labels/edges were not treated as vulnerability verdicts.

The snapshot sits immediately after the 12.0.16 release, which strongly suggests the target is the first post-release security fix, but I could not identify that fix from source alone; memory-based comparison against later Jetty releases was intentionally avoided as unverifiable.

Large portions of the codebase (HTTP/2/3 internals, WebSocket, QUIC, OSGi, JSP/Maven tooling, integrations, and docs) were reviewed only by targeted searches; the absence of a candidate is not proof that no vulnerability exists.

No candidate is submitted because none of the examined leads had a demonstrated attacker-controlled input reaching a security-relevant sink without contradicting counterevidence; this is an evidence-threshold decision, not a claim that the snapshot is clean.

rejected_leads.lead: Alias-check semantics: ContextHandler.checkAlias approves a resource if ANY AliasCheck approves (OR), and the default SymlinkAllowedResourceAliasChecker approves symlinks whose alias path is not a protected target (AllowedResourceAliasChecker.java:139-221, SymlinkAllowedResourceAliasChecker.java:47-117, ContextHandler.java:1314-1336).
rejected_leads.reason: This is the documented Jetty 12 design ('allow symlinks to arbitrary targets so long as the symlink file is not protected'); the restrictive AllowedResourceAliasChecker added by ResourceServlet for custom bases cannot tighten the OR-ed result, but no attacker-controlled input produces a resource outside the intended, documented access policy under default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: Protected-target matching in ContextHandler.isProtectedTarget / setProtectedTargets (ContextHandler.java:1226-1261) only compacts paths beginning with '//' and matches the canonical (encoded) path; encoded-slash requests such as /WEB-INF%2Fweb.xml are not matched as protected targets and can be decoded by Paths.get() during resource resolution.
rejected_leads.reason: Such URIs carry UriCompliance.Violation.AMBIGUOUS_PATH_SEPARATOR and are rejected with 400 under the default UriCompliance (UriCompliance.java:175-187; HttpChannelState.java:637-645). Only explicitly documented 'unsafe/legacy' compliance modes (LEGACY/UNSAFE) allow it, which Jetty warns must be audited; no default-config bypass was established.

rejected_leads.lead: ee10/ee9 ErrorHandler.badMessageError builds an HTML body ('Bad Message ...reason: ' + reason) with Content-Type text/html without escaping reason (jetty-ee10 ErrorHandler.java:528-536, jetty-ee9 ErrorHandler.java:518-526; invoked from ee9 HttpChannel.java:956-962).
rejected_leads.reason: Traced BadMessageException reasons used on request-parsing failures (HttpParser, CookieCache/RFC6265CookieParser, MultiPart, ForwardedRequestCustomizer, HttpTokens.Token) — they are static strings or a single quoted token character, not full attacker-controlled markup. The equivalent core method is deprecated and no longer invoked (core ErrorHandler.java:426-433). No reliable injection path found.

rejected_leads.lead: ShutdownHandler matches the shutdown path with String.startsWith instead of equality (ShutdownHandler.java:133,141), and builds the security decision on the remote socket address (ShutdownHandler.java:178-188).
rejected_leads.reason: The secret token check and the loopback check are always enforced before shutdown; prefix matching only widens which URLs are treated as shutdown attempts. Robustness/consistency issue, no auth bypass demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: SecuredRedirectHandler constructs the Location header from the request Host via Request.getServerName (SecuredRedirectHandler.java:96-106) — potential host-header poisoning/open redirect.
rejected_leads.reason: This is long-standing upstream behavior; a victim's browser sets Host to the real server, so impact is limited to cache-poisoning/misconfigured-proxy scenarios, and it is a configuration-visible design property, not a clear repository vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: CrossOriginHandler echoes the full, unvalidated Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin / Timing-Allow-Origin (CrossOriginHandler.java:460-486) and the setAllowedOriginPatterns javadoc says the default is '*' while the field default is an empty set (CrossOriginHandler.java:68,181).
rejected_leads.reason: The Origin header is browser-controlled (script cannot set arbitrary space-separated origins), so the echo does not create a cross-origin bypass; the doc/default mismatch is a documentation/behavior inconsistency, not a vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsing: base XmlParser does not disable external entities/FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING (XmlParser.java:111-119,150-193), and WebDescriptor.WebDescriptorParser (ee9/ee10 WebDescriptor.java:93-103) does not override configure(), unlike XmlConfiguration.ConfigurationParser (XmlConfiguration.java:2075-2113).
rejected_leads.reason: Only local/supply-chain-controlled documents (WEB-INF/web.xml, web-fragment.xml inside deployed JARs) are parsed by that path; a remote unauthenticated trigger was not found, and catalog entity resolvers are in place. Threshold not met as a remote vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: JwtDecoder.decode does not verify the JWT signature (JwtDecoder.java:62-66), and AbstractLoginService.validate is a no-op unless _fullValidate is enabled (AbstractLoginService.java:35,115-120).
rejected_leads.reason: Both are documented Jetty/OIDC designs (signature validation replaced by TLS validation of the token endpoint; full validation is an opt-in configuration), with no attacker-controlled bypass demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultSessionIdManager falls back to java.util.Random for session IDs if SecureRandom cannot be instantiated (DefaultSessionIdManager.java:349-366).
rejected_leads.reason: Fallback only occurs when SecureRandom creation throws (heavily degraded JVM), and it is accompanied by a warning; not remotely triggerable.

summary: Snapshot reviewed: Eclipse Jetty main branch at 12.0.17-SNAPSHOT (root pom line 7), i.e. immediately after the 12.0.16 release (VERSION.txt line 3, "jetty-12.0.16 - 09 December 2024", with an empty 12.0.17-SNAPSHOT section) — this is exactly the window in which Jetty normally lands the first security fix of a new patch cycle. I reviewed request-handling, path/canonicalization, resource-serving/alias-check, security/authentication, session/cookie, HTTP/1.1/2/3 parsing, XML, start/config, and proxy components, plus the duplicate ee9/ee10 implementations and the integration modules. I could not identify, from source evidence alone, a defect with attacker-controlled input reaching a security-relevant sink with concrete impact, so no candidate meets the requested evidence threshold. The most likely ground-truth issue for this snapshot (the externally reported vulnerability fixed in the immediately following release) could not be pinned to a specific code path without the fix diff or tests, which are not present in scope.
